newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol down on upcoming offer, '96 results.
newsitem.headline: Repsol down on upcoming offer, '96 results.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Repsol were sharply lower on Thursday as the market started to focus on the upcoming sale of the government's remaining stake in the energy firm, dealers and analysts said.
Analysts said 1996 results, released yesterday, were basically good, and had met most Spanish analysts forecasts. But some U.S. estimates may have been undershot.
Dealers said there was also a large sell order in the market, thought to be from a U.S. fund and possibly related to the sale of the government's last 10 percent stake in the firm, due this quarter.
At 1120 GMT, Repsol was down 110 pesetas, 1.94 percent, to 5,560 while the Ibex-35 index was up 0.26 percent, to 5,293.66.

"The results don't look too bad at the operating level, but there may have been some scope for disappointment from U.S. houses as some of them revised up their 1996 profits forecasts fairly recently," said an analyst who requested anonymity.
Repsol's 1996 net attributable profit rose 1.1 percent to 119.1 billion pesetas.
The analyst said the upcoming privatisation was "bound to see weakness in the shares on the prospect of more supply."
"It's good for the firm in a way because price weakness basically guarantees the success of the issue," he added.
One dealer said a large sell order was also sapping the stock amid relatively thin volume.

"For some time there's been a very big sell order, probably from an American fund that is either switching or reducing its stake before subscribing to the new offer. It's more noticeable because (trading) volumes are thinner," he said.
